title: Exact natural transformations through derived finite totals and exact postcomposition
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] in fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention], using ordinary derived categories and K-injective right derived functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive], $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ and $P:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ additive exact functors, and $\theta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\to H$ a specified natural transformation. Let $K:\Delta\to\operatorname{Ch}^{\ge0}(\mathcal A)$ be a strict cosimplicial complex, where $\Delta$ has finite nonempty ordered sets and monotone maps. Put $T(K)^r=\bigoplus_{n+q=r}K^{n,q}$ with differential $\delta+(-1)^nd$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], and let $Q$ denote localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Let $M\in D(\mathcal A)$ and $a:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QT(K)$. Denote termwise exact descent by $H_D,P_D$ and the descended transformation by $\theta_D$.
The termwise maps $e^{n,q}=\theta_{K^{n,q}}$ form a strict cosimplicial chain map $e:K\to HK$. The canonical finite-biproduct identification $E:H(TK)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(HK)$ satisfies $E\theta_{TK}=T(e)$ and, after localization,
$$Q(E)\,H_D(a)\,\theta_{D,M}=QT(e)\,a.$$
There are compatible nonnegative resolutions of $K,HK,e$ giving natural isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal C)$
$$u:P_DRG(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_n P_DRG(QK^n),\qquad w:P_DRG(H_DM)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_n P_DRG(H_DQK^n)$$
for which
$$w\,P_DRG(\theta_{D,M})=\operatorname{Tot}_nP_DRG(\theta_{D,QK^n})\,u.$$
The comparisons $u,w$ are respectively $P_D(\chi_{G,K})\circ P_DRG(a)$ and $P_D(\chi_{G,HK})\circ P_DRG(Q(E)H_D(a))$, where $\chi$ is the canonical derived finite-total comparison of [lem-sfb-nonnegative-derived-totalization] and $P_D$ is moved inside the total by the canonical finite-biproduct identifications. They are independent of compatible resolution choices and natural in maps of $K,M,a$. They preserve specified augmentations and their actual maps; for a strict augmentation by a nonnegative complex, their composite with its derived augmentation is its totalized columnwise derived augmentation. Every total has finite diagonals: with an added resolution index $s$, its terms have $n,q,s\ge0$ and $n+q+s=r$. For any further exact additive functor $S:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ to a Grothendieck abelian category with its ordinary derived category, the corresponding comparisons for $SP$ are the images under $S_D$ of this entire square, using the canonical finite-biproduct identifications, including augmentations. In particular this applies to exact module restriction to a slice site with its pulled-back ring. Neither $H$ nor $P$ nor $S$ is required to preserve injectives; no unbounded product totalization occurs.

proof.text: Naturality of exactNonnegativeLocalizationIso follows from mapDerivedCategoryFactors and mapExtendIso. Combine it with summandwise beta naturality to obtain naturality of exactFiniteTotalLocalizationIso. Apply P_D to comparisonG.naturality and precompose by the given model isomorphisms. This proves the general postcomparison naturality equation. Substitute localized_unit to obtain the unit square.

proof.text: The nonnegative derived unit is natural by extension-by-zero naturality and rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ_naturality. On a termwise injective nonnegative complex it is invertible, since the extension is bounded below injective, hence K-injective. Cancel this unit against comparisonG.column_normalized to obtain the column square. Apply P_D and the exact localization naturality. Apply P_D also to comparisonG.augmentation and move P through the finite total by beta; this yields the specified actual augmentation maps.

proof.text: For S, choose the existing comparisons for S and P followed by S. Check beta composition on every finite summand. Check the composition law for mapExtendIso in each degree, then combine it with mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac to prove the nonnegative exact localization composition law. These identities give exactFiniteTotalLocalizationIso composition. Naturality of the derived composition isomorphism identifies the composite and iterated postcomparisons. Apply S_D to the already proved unit square and use finite-total naturality for the further square. All totals retain their original finite nonnegative diagonals.
